what_happened: The queue drain stalled and could not work any item after any change to athena.toml. The operator ran the fix for the drain's re-read-after-config-change problem directly, ahead of Athena's plan, so the queue could move again. No job was attached to the event.
cause: The drain treats config as something loaded in a way that does not tolerate a later change. Config changes are a routine result of jobs, including jobs the drain itself runs, yet no test covers a drain that continues across an athena.toml change. The plan did not rank this failure as urgent. The fix only happened when it blocked everything and the operator stepped in. The earlier config-schema case (w348) shows config changes already interact badly with the running binary, and that was handled one symptom at a time.
prevention: Add an automated test that runs the drain through a queue where a job changes athena.toml mid-drain, in both valid and invalid cases. The drain must re-read the config, then continue with the next item or stop with a clear error naming the config problem. The test must run as a required check on every change to the drain or config loader. The drain should also check at startup and after each job that the config parses, so it stops visibly instead of stalling.
proposed_request: Make the queue drain keep working after athena.toml changes. After each job, the drain must re-read athena.toml. If the file parses, it continues with the next queued item using the new values. If it does not parse, it stops cleanly and reports which field failed, without losing or stranding any queued item. Add automated tests that run a multi-item drain where an earlier job edits athena.toml, covering a valid edit, an edit that adds a field the schema does not know, and a file that is malformed. Each test must show the drain either works the next item or stops with the clear error. Run these tests as part of the standard checks so any later change that brings back the stall is caught before merge.
